Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- 6 weeks of generalized fatigue and diffuse aches (shoulders, back, hips, knees) without joint swelling; decreased appetite without weight change; intermittent headaches; no respiratory, GI, or GU symptoms; no neurological deficits.
- Notable history: U.S. travel with outdoor exposure (shorts), followed by transient non-itchy rash on calf that resolved; possible sore throat and mild feverish feeling around that time.
- Past history: Asthma and hay fever; stable.
- Working diagnosis and considerations (aligned with DDx and transcript):
  - Possible Lyme disease (early localized/disseminated): Exposure context and erythema migrans–like rash with subsequent systemic symptoms. Plan: Lyme serology; treat with appropriate antibiotics if positive as discussed.
  - Post-viral illness/post-viral fatigue: Sore throat and low-grade fever around onset could explain prolonged fatigue/myalgias.
  - Other causes of fatigue to screen: Hypothyroidism, anemia, vitamin D deficiency (screening labs considered; only CBC, renal, liver, and Lyme serology explicitly planned in transcript).
- Plan per transcript: Arrange blood tests through support line (CBC, renal and liver function, Lyme serology). Phone follow-up about one week after tests. Antibiotics if Lyme positive.
- No red flags elicited (no focal neuro deficits, no cardiorespiratory or GI alarm features).

- Arrange follow-up: Phone review ~1 week after blood draw to discuss results and next steps.
